summary: KIPP - Earth Trend helps people investigate changes in Earth-system variables using NASA Earth-data products. Choose a variable, region, and time range, inspect a monthly time series, and examine its rate of change with uncertainty and significance context. The project identifies data provenance, units, coverage, and limitations so that reanalysis and other derived products are not mistaken for direct observations.
details:
KIPP - Earth Trend

KIPP - Earth Trend helps students, educators, and curious explorers investigate how Earth changes across regions and over time. Choose a variable, region, and period, follow its monthly history, and examine its rate of change with uncertainty and statistical evidence.

Aplication: Open the application

Github: Explore the source code

Explore the application

Explore - follow changes across the globe

Start by choosing a variable, region, and time range. The globe displays the selected monthly field, while playback lets you follow its evolution. Global and regional charts show how values change over time, helping you connect a spatial pattern with its history. Variable details explain the source, units, and available coverage.

Compare - investigate places and periods side by side

Set up panels A and B with the regions and periods you want to study. Their globe cameras stay synchronized, and matching variables share consistent colors. Inspect the corresponding time series and trend estimates, or copy one panel's settings to the other as a starting point for a comparison.

Trend Lab - build a focused investigation

Choose a region, one or two indicators, a study period, and a reference period, then select Generate investigation. Three views help answer different questions about the same data.

Trend shows the direction and rate of change, with fitted lines, sample counts, confidence intervals, and significance where the available record supports inference. Change controls let you examine the estimated change over a chosen interval.


Anomalies shows how each month differs from the corresponding month in the selected reference period. Switch between original values, departures in physical units, and standardized departures to explore unusual conditions.

Relationships compares two indicators through time-series charts, a scatterplot, and lag analysis. Users can explore whether the indicators vary together and how that association changes when one series precedes the other by a selected number of months.

Events - start with a historical context

Browse historical events and use the available regions and periods as starting points for exploration. Monthly fields provide environmental context around the selected event. Availability depends on the underlying product and its coverage.

Guide - understand the investigation steps

Guide introduces the application workflow and explains how to read variables, time series, trends, and statistical evidence. It helps users understand the choices and limitations behind an investigation.

AI assistant - ask questions as you explore

The integrated assistant helps explain available indicators and application controls, and supports questions about the current investigation. Its explanations can be checked against the displayed values, source information, and method notes.

Save and export your investigation

Save investigation settings to revisit them on the same device. CSV and JSON exports retain the data and provenance needed to continue the analysis, document the selected region and period, or discuss results in class.

What benefits does it offer?

KIPP connects a visible pattern on a globe to the monthly records and statistical analysis behind it. Students can ask a question, compare places, and develop an explanation supported by data. Educators can use the same workflow to introduce time series, seasonal variation, uncertainty, and significance.

The intended impact is to make Earth-data investigation more approachable in classrooms and independent learning. Exportable results and source metadata allow users to revisit their choices and discuss how the region, period, and product affect their interpretation.

What data makes it possible?

The processing pipeline brings together global products and regional catalogs across several Earth-system domains. Extraction starts in 2000 where available and extends to each product's latest available month. Effective dates and coverage vary by indicator.

  • NASA MERRA-2: Atmospheric reanalysis covering temperature, humidity, winds, pressure, fluxes, clouds, aerosols, and chemistry.
  • NASA GPM IMERG: Precipitation estimates and liquid-phase probability, preserving Final and Late processing provenance.
  • NASA MODIS Terra MOD13C2: Monthly NDVI and EVI vegetation indices with quality information
  • NASA/JPL GRACE and GRACE-FO: Mass anomalies for water-storage and large-scale ice-mass investigations.
  • NOAA/NSIDC Sea Ice Index: Arctic and Antarctic sea-ice concentration and derived extent masks.
  • NASA COOLR: Events and Reports layers processed into separate monthly catalog record counts.

Each investigation uses the indicators and months available in the application catalog. Product-level links and processing descriptions are collected in the

What makes the approach creative?

The modules offer connected ways to investigate one question. Spatial playback reveals where patterns appear, comparison shows how places or periods differ, and Trend Lab examines changes and relationships quantitatively. Historical contexts and guided explanations help users choose a starting point, while exports carry the investigation into their own work.

What factors shaped the design?

  • Traceability Product identities, units, coverage, and transformations accompany the data and exports.
  • Scientific interpretation Labels distinguish satellite estimates, reanalysis, model diagnostics, and catalog records. Methods expose assumptions and uncertainty.
  • Geographic meaning Regional selections use bounding rectangles. Spatial aggregation and coverage influence the resulting series.
  • Missing and limited data Gaps remain visible, and inference requires sufficient valid samples. Product availability determines the questions users can investigate.
  • Responsible communication Statistical significance, association, and fitted change are interpreted within the selected method and period. Event records carry reporting limitations.

Credits and AI use

NASA and NOAA/NSIDC products supply the scientific inputs. NASA Blue Marble provides the static globe background, and Natural Earth boundaries provide geographic context. OpenAI Codex assisted implementation and documentation. ImageGen generated mascot artwork, and the application includes a Gemini-based assistant. Generated material and final scientific interpretations require team review

NASA MODIS Terra MOD13C2.061 — Monthly NDVI and EVI vegetation indices with quality information
NASA/JPL GRACE and GRACE-FO RL06.3Mv04 — Mass anomalies for water-storage and ice-mass investigations
NASA COOLR — Landslide Events and Reports processed as separate monthly catalog record counts
